newsitem.title: USA: Ultramar to expand new Okla refinery - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Ultramar to expand new Okla refinery - CEO.

text.p: Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp, which Tuesday said it is buying French major Total SA's North American downstream assets for $811 million, plans to expand the Total refinery in Ardmore, Okla., the company's chief executive officer told Reuters.
He said Ultramar would likely take about two years and spend from $15-$25 million to expand the refinery's crude throughput to about 85,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 68,000 bpd currently.
"I think we can get it there in about two years," Roger Hemminghaus said in a telephone interview Wednesday, adding due diligence related to the deal will clarify his forecast.

The deal includes three Total refineries with about 150,000 bpd current crude throughput capacity, as well as marketing and retail assets in Colorado, Kansas, Oklahoma and Michigan, and raises Ultramar's North American throughput capacity to about 650,000 bpd.

Asked if any of the Total assets had any strings of vulnerability attached, Hemminghaus said Total has spent hundreds of millions of dollars in the last several years upgrading its refineries and shut one plant in Kansas.
He said those capital projects included about $250 million in upgrades at the Ardmore refinery aimed in part at running cheaper West Texas Sour (WTS) crude oil.
"I think we can add significant value by increasing throughput and running the cheaper crude," the Ultramar chief said referring to the Oklahoma plant.

He said the other two refineries, one in Denver and one in Alma, Michigan are both in niche markets, where competitive concerns are not as acute as in Oklahoma, which is on the edge of the dense and fiercely competitive U.S. Gulf "refinery row" market.

Hemminghaus reiterated his view that refiners in the Gulf Coast market find their per barrel costs flatten out markedly above the 75,000 bpd of crude throughput threshold. The Oklahoma refinery will rise above that level with the upgrade.
